quests.instruction: Now try 'quick'. q has a tail, and k is tall.
quests.question: quick
quests.hint: q is a circle with a straight tail. Then u, i (dot), c, k (tall). Write the dot last.
quests.explanation: q always travels with u in English. The two letters together sit close, but u stays on the line.
quests.funFact: In old English, the word 'quick' meant 'alive'.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'quiet'. It has q, u, i, e and t.
quests.question: quiet
quests.hint: Tail on q, then u and i with its dot, e, and t with a cross. Check that the circle of q is closed.
quests.explanation: Five letters with a tail, a dot and a cross. Writing the details last keeps your pen moving.
quests.funFact: When you whisper, your throat does not vibrate the way it does when you speak out loud.

quests.instruction: Write 'queen' on the line. It has two e's and q with a tail.
quests.question: queen
quests.hint: q, u, e, e, n. The two e's are the same size and closed. The tail on q goes below the line.
quests.explanation: Two e's in a row should look like a pair. Check that both are closed circles.
quests.funFact: A beehive usually has one queen bee, who lays all of the eggs.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'jumping'. It has a j, a tail on p and a tail on g.
quests.question: jumping
quests.hint: j has a hook and a dot, then u, m, p (tail), i (dot), n, g (tail). Three letters go below the line.
quests.explanation: Three descenders in one word. Keep the tails the same length so they don't crash into each other.
quests.funFact: Adding -ing to a word shows that something is happening right now.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'running'. It has a double n and ends in -ing.
quests.question: running
quests.hint: r, u, n, n, i, n, g. Three n's: make every arch the same size. The tail of g is the only part below the line.
quests.explanation: Three arches in a row, with the i between them. Check that the arches are even.
quests.funFact: Humans are not the fastest runners, but they are very good at running long distances.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'playing'. It has p, l, y and g, so tails and a tall l.
quests.question: playing
quests.hint: p (tail), l (tall), a, y (tail), i (dot), n, g (tail). Three tails and one tall stem.
quests.explanation: A seven-letter word with lots of parts. Write the whole word before you add the dot.
quests.funFact: Young animals, like puppies and kittens, learn a lot by playing.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'sunshine' onto your line. It is the words 'sun' and 'shine' joined together.
quests.question: sunshine
quests.hint: s, u, n, s, h, i, n, e. Write 'sun', then 'shine' right after it without a gap. h is the only tall letter.
quests.explanation: A compound word is two words with no gap between them. Keep the letters evenly spaced across all eight.
quests.funFact: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach the Earth.

quests.instruction: Now try 'rainbow'. It is the words 'rain' and 'bow' joined together.
quests.question: rainbow
quests.hint: r, a, i, n, b, o, w. Write 'rain' first, then 'bow' with a tall b. Add the dot on i at the end.
quests.explanation: A seven-letter word split into two easy parts. Take them one at a time.
quests.funFact: In a rainbow, red is on the outside and violet is on the inside.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'football'. It is 'foot' and 'ball' joined together.
quests.question: football
quests.hint: f, o, o, t, b, a, l, l. Keep their tops at the same height and the o's identical. Remember: tall stems (f, b, l) reach the top line.
quests.explanation: Many tall letters in one word. Check their tops are at the same height.
quests.funFact: Football is played in almost every country in the world.

quests.instruction: Write the two words 'ice cream', with a clear gap between them.
quests.question: ice cream
quests.hint: Write 'ice', leave a gap the size of an o, then 'cream'. Remember the dot on i.
quests.explanation: Two short words with a gap between them. A gap that is too small makes them look like one word.
quests.funFact: Ice cream has to be stirred while it freezes, so the ice crystals stay small and smooth.

quests.instruction: Write the two words 'school bag'.
quests.question: school bag
quests.hint: Write 'school' with its tall h and l, a gap, then 'bag' with a tall b and a tail on g.
quests.explanation: Two words, seven letters in the first and three in the second. Keep the same size throughout.
quests.funFact: A heavy school bag is best carried on both shoulders.

quests.instruction: Write the words 'good night' with an equal gap between them.
quests.question: good night
quests.hint: Write 'good', leave a gap, then 'night' with its tall h and t and its tailed g. Add the dot at the end.
quests.explanation: Two words, with tails and tall letters mixed. This is a phrase that you would really write.
quests.funFact: Sleep helps children's bodies and brains to grow.

quests.instruction: Write the phrase 'a big red balloon'. Keep all four words the same size.
quests.question: a big red balloon
quests.hint: Four words with equal gaps. Match the sizes of the two b's. Remember: tall stems (b, d, l) reach the top line and tails (g) drop below the baseline.
quests.explanation: Four words on one line. Check that your last word is the same size as your first.
quests.funFact: The first people to fly in a hot air balloon did so in France in 1783.

quests.instruction: Write the phrase 'two little birds', keeping an even slant and size.
quests.question: two little birds
quests.hint: Three words with many tall letters. b, d and both l's reach the top line, while the t's stop a little lower. Keep the tall ones parallel.
quests.explanation: A line with many tall stems is a good check of consistency. Keep them parallel.
quests.funFact: A hummingbird can flap its wings dozens of times every second.

quests.instruction: Write the phrase 'green leaves and blue sky'. Keep the baseline level.
quests.question: green leaves and blue sky
quests.hint: Five words. The line should not slope up or down. Remember: tall stems (l, d, b, k) reach the top line and tails (g, y) drop below the baseline.
quests.explanation: A longer line asks you to keep the baseline straight, and the gaps equal, from start to finish.
quests.funFact: Leaves change color in autumn because the green substance in them breaks down.

quests.instruction: Write the sentence 'The cat sat.' Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
quests.question: The cat sat.
quests.hint: Capital T, then 'he', a gap, 'cat', a gap, 'sat'. Finish with a dot sitting on the baseline.
quests.explanation: A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. The dot shows where the thought ends.
quests.funFact: The full stop is called a period in American English.

quests.instruction: Copy this sentence: 'Dogs can run.' Don't forget the capital D and the full stop.
quests.question: Dogs can run.
quests.hint: Capital D has a stem and a big curve. Then 'ogs', a gap, 'can', a gap, 'run'. End with a dot.
quests.explanation: The capital D is the only tall letter at the start. The rest of the line is small, with a tail on g.
quests.funFact: Greyhounds can run faster than sixty kilometers an hour.

quests.instruction: Now write 'I like milk.' Notice that I is a capital on its own.
quests.question: I like milk.
quests.hint: Capital I has two small bars. Then 'like' and 'milk' with tall l, k, l, k. End with a dot.
quests.explanation: The word 'I' is always a capital letter, and the sentence starts with it. Keep it clear from the small l that comes next.
quests.funFact: Ancient Greek scholars used dots to show where to pause when reading aloud.

quests.instruction: Try this sentence: 'I am Maya.' Both I and Maya need capital letters.
quests.question: I am Maya.
quests.hint: Capital I, a gap, 'am', a gap, capital M and 'aya'. End with a full stop after the a.
quests.explanation: Capital letters appear twice here: at the start of the sentence and at the start of a name.
quests.funFact: Some languages, such as Chinese and Japanese, do not use capital letters at all.

quests.instruction: Write 'Ravi and I play.' on one neat line. Both Ravi and I are capitals.
quests.question: Ravi and I play.
quests.hint: Capital R, 'avi', a gap, 'and', a gap, capital I, a gap, 'play' with a tail on p and y. End with a dot.
quests.explanation: The word 'I' is always a capital, even in the middle of a sentence.
quests.funFact: In English it is polite to name the other person first, as in 'Ravi and I'.

quests.instruction: Write the sentence 'Maya and I read.' Keep the capitals clearly bigger than the small letters.
quests.question: Maya and I read.
quests.hint: Capital M, 'aya', gap, 'and', gap, capital I, gap, 'read', then a dot. Make the capitals the same height.
quests.explanation: Capitals are taller than the small letters. Check that M and I match in height.
quests.funFact: The first picture book for children, 'Orbis Pictus', was published in 1658.

quests.instruction: Write the question 'Who is it?' End with a question mark.
quests.question: Who is it?
quests.hint: Capital W (four slants), then 'ho', gap, 'is', gap, 'it'. For the question mark: curve over, curve down, then a dot beneath it.
quests.explanation: A question ends with a question mark, not a full stop. Make the curve first, then the dot at the bottom.
quests.funFact: One idea is that the question mark comes from the Latin word 'quaestio', which means question.

quests.instruction: Write the question 'Can I play?' End with a question mark.
quests.question: Can I play?
quests.hint: Capital C, 'an', gap, capital I, gap, 'play' with tails on p and y. Finish with the hooked line and the dot.
quests.explanation: Capital I in the middle of the sentence is a capital because it means 'me'.
quests.funFact: In Spanish, a question begins with an upside-down question mark, like this: ¿

quests.instruction: Write the question 'Is it red?' with a question mark at the end.
quests.question: Is it red?
quests.hint: Capital I, small s, gap, 'it', gap, 'red', then the question mark. The tall d in red and the question mark are about the same height.
quests.explanation: Three short words and a question mark. Keep the mark the same height as your capital letters.
quests.funFact: In Greek, the question mark looks like a semicolon.

quests.instruction: Copy this sentence: 'Look at that!' End with an exclamation mark.
quests.question: Look at that!
quests.hint: Capital L is a corner. Then 'ook', gap, 'at', gap, 'that'. For the exclamation mark, draw a tall line and a dot below it.
quests.explanation: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling or a shout. The line is straight and the dot sits on the baseline.
quests.funFact: Printers sometimes call the exclamation mark a 'bang'.

quests.instruction: Now write 'I won!' It is short, but has a capital and an exclamation mark.
quests.question: I won!
quests.hint: Capital I, gap, then 'won', then the exclamation mark. The dot of the mark sits on the baseline.
quests.explanation: A short sentence has the same rules as a long one: a capital at the start and a mark at the end.
quests.funFact: Old typewriters had no exclamation mark key. Typists typed a full stop, backed up, and typed an apostrophe above it.

quests.instruction: Try this sentence: 'What a day!' with an exclamation mark.
quests.question: What a day!
quests.hint: Capital W, 'hat', gap, 'a', gap, 'day' with a tail on y, then the mark. Keep the words close to the same size.
quests.explanation: Three words and a mark at the end. Check your gaps and the height of the exclamation line.
quests.funFact: Comic books use exclamation marks very often to show action and surprise.

quests.instruction: Write the list 'red, blue, green'. Put a comma after each word except the last.
quests.question: red, blue, green
quests.hint: The comma is a small dot with a tail that curves down to the left. It sits on the baseline right after the last letter, before the gap.
quests.explanation: A comma separates items in a list. It touches the word before it, and then there is a gap.
quests.funFact: The word 'comma' comes from a Greek word that means 'a piece cut off'.

quests.instruction: Write the list 'milk, rice, eggs'. Put the commas right after the words.
quests.question: milk, rice, eggs
quests.hint: Write 'milk' then the comma straight away. Then a gap, 'rice', comma, gap, 'eggs'. g has a tail.
quests.explanation: Commas stay close to the word before them, not the word after. The gaps come after the comma.
quests.funFact: A printer in Venice named Aldus Manutius gave the comma its modern look around 1500.

quests.instruction: Write the list 'cats, dogs, birds'. The commas keep the animals separate.
quests.question: cats, dogs, birds
quests.hint: Comma touches the end of 'cats', then a gap, 'dogs', comma, gap, 'birds'. Keep the commas small.
quests.explanation: In a list, the comma tells the reader to take a short pause before the next item.
quests.funFact: In some countries, a comma is used as the decimal point in numbers, so 3,5 means three and a half.
